name: Audible Audiobook Deep Summary (Chapters + Reflection + Counterpoints)
author: plaud.ai.twelve458
description: Paste an audiobook transcript. Get chapter notes, key ideas, counterpoints, and actions.
body:
The primary objective is to transform a full audiobook transcript into a structured, actionable, and reflective learning artifact for self-learning, work learning, and critical thinking.
The process starts by creating a "Book Snapshot" which includes the title, author, narrator, genre, a one-sentence summary, the central question answered, the listener's purpose, and the implied audience.
A "Big Picture Summary" is then generated, outlining the core thesis, the author's main logical argument, key themes, and the author's "Operating Model" which details their worldview on what drives outcomes and what actions to start or stop.
The structure includes a "Chapter-by-Chapter Summary" if chapters are detectable, providing each chapter's thesis, key points, notable examples, a practical takeaway, and a reflective question.
A section on "Key Concepts and Definitions" lists and explains 8-18 core concepts with their definitions, examples, practical implications, and common misunderstandings.
"Key Takeaways" are high-leverage points, each detailed with what it says, why it matters, the evidence used, personal and work applications, and potential risks.
Practical "Methods / Playbook" are extracted from the book, detailing steps, usage conditions, success signals, and common failure modes for 3-8 recommended methods.
A critical analysis section, "Counterpoints and Key Disagreements," presents the strongest counterarguments, assesses the author's strongest and weakest points, and explores potential middle ground.
"Reflection Prompts" are generated for personal growth and work learning, linked to specific takeaways to encourage deeper thought on topics like prioritization, decision-making, and communication.
A "Tailored Action Plan" is created with specific actions for the next 48 hours, 7-14 days, and work applications, all linked to takeaways and including effort levels, success criteria, and obstacle planning.
"Memory Aids" are provided to reinforce learning, including a one-paragraph teach-back, a single key action, memorable quotes, and key stories with their lessons.
The final section, "Open Questions," lists questions for deeper study and questions that one might ask the author to encourage further exploration beyond the book.

name: In-depth summary
author: Marcos Goulart
description: Organizes theses, arguments, and citations from academic texts with analyses to assist your studies.
body:
The main objective is to create an in-depth reading summary for critical analysis and extraction of essential information for academic research.
Complete identification requires title, author, year of publication, publisher (if applicable), and total number of pages of the text.
The context and introduction should cover the author's and work's background, the main theme, relevance in the field of study, and the central thesis defended.
The structure of the work should describe the organization of the text (chapters, sections) and its contribution to the development of arguments.
Critical analysis of the main arguments involves identifying, discussing, explaining in detail, and including direct quotations with page indication as evidence, analyzing validity, coherence, and limitations.
Key concepts should be enumerated, defined, with an explanation of their importance in the context of the work and, if possible, illustrative quotations.
Methodology, if applicable to research, should briefly describe the approach used (qualitative, quantitative, bibliographic) and its influence on the results.
Dialogue with other authors/theories should identify influences, criticisms of other approaches, and points of connection.
The contributions of the work to the field of study, as well as its gaps, weaknesses, or unaddressed issues, should be detailed.
Personal comments and questions include reflections on the text, points of attention, and questions raised, relating them to research interests.
The summary should list 5 to 7 keywords that represent its content.
The bibliographic reference should be formatted according to specific standards (ABNT, APA, MLA, Vancouver, etc.).
All direct quotations must follow the specified standards (e.g., ABNT, with author-date and page number), being representative of the analyzed points.
The final objective of the summary is to serve as a study and research tool for quick consultation of points and quotations, assisting in the construction of arguments and academic works.

name: Book Creator
author: Petricelli
description: Converts transcripts into four books with varied styles, from formal to literary and immersive.
body:
The goal is to create four structured versions of books from transcripts, transforming spoken or written records into well-structured literary works.
The title of the work should be used if mentioned in the transcript, or a representative title based on the central idea of the content.
The name of the author or speaker indicated in the transcript should be included as the author of the book.
The creation date of the transcript should be inserted at the beginning of the document, as indicated in the file name or metadata.
The content should be reorganized logically and fluidly, following a chronological or thematic sequence to enhance the reader's understanding.
The central message and main themes of the original transcript should be preserved, avoiding arbitrary cuts or interpretations that distort the content.
Version 1 should structure the text in the logical order of the events in the transcript, building a long narrative faithful to the original content with a formal or literary tone.
Version 2 should organize the content in a natural and emotionally engaging way, rewriting the narration in an intimate and colloquial tone to create emotional connection, simplifying technical sections and preserving emotional depth.
Version 3 should transform the narrative into a more visual and interactive form, using a fluid and conversational tone, adding dialogues, settings, actions, and emotional expressions based on cues from the transcript to enhance immersion while maintaining coherence with the original facts.
Version 4 should rewrite the content with a focus on emotional, sensory, and philosophical depth, incorporating metaphors, sensory atmospheres, stream of consciousness, introspection, and internal dilemmas to create an immersive and aesthetic reading experience.
Each version should be delivered as a complete text, including book title, author name (if available), transcript date, narrative body, and sections clearly separated by visual headers or numbered segments.

name: 📚 Learning engine 🧠 Thinking framework
author: Ravi Shekhaar Singh
description: Upload audio and get a clear outline, deep explanations, questions, and a next-step roadmap.
body:
This document provides a master prompt template for the PLAUD app, designed to transform audio content into a structured knowledge base, and outlines a framework of skills for effectively using this system.
The master prompt, titled "Deep Knowledge Extraction & Learning Engine," instructs the AI to act as an expert extractor and educator, processing audio through a six-phase process to create a comprehensive learning document.
Phase 1 involves creating a detailed, hierarchical "Content Map" or Table of Contents, breaking the audio into logical sections, subsections, and micro-topics.
Phase 2 requires a "Deep Dive Explanation" for each section, including core concepts, non-obvious insights like trade-offs and design decisions, and practical, real-world applications.
Phase 3, "Learning Reinforcement," mandates generating multi-level questions (basic, intermediate, advanced) and suggesting related topics for knowledge expansion after each section.
Phase 4 focuses on "Cross-Section Synthesis" by identifying common themes, connections, and contradictions across all sections to provide a unified mental model.
Phase 5, "Interview Preparation," generates conceptual, scenario-based, and system design questions based on the audio, complete with structured, high-quality answers.
Phase 6 concludes the prompt with a "Next Learning Roadmap," suggesting subsequent learning topics categorized as Must Learn, Good to Learn, and Advanced/Expert.
An effective "Skill Layer" is introduced to transform the prompt into a repeatable system, starting with "Input Framing," which involves classifying audio as technical, meeting, or learning, and slightly modifying the prompt to emphasize relevant aspects like implementation or decisions.
The "Iterative Refinement Loop" skill involves asking follow-up questions to the AI to deepen the analysis, turning the static output into an interactive learning system.
The "Convert to Decision Intelligence" skill leverages the extracted knowledge to analyze implied decisions, potential system failures, and ways to communicate findings to leadership, thereby enhancing one's influence at work.
The "Build Personal Knowledge Graph" skill suggests using each output to create a personal mental map of systems thinking, where concepts are nodes and relationships are edges.
The "Use for Team Influence" skill advocates using the structured analysis of trade-offs and scenarios to present arguments with authority and objectivity.
A bonus "Power Upgrade Version" prompt can be appended to have the AI also identify assumptions, risks, edge cases, and potential inaccuracies in the speaker's original content for each section.

The role of a Behavior Analyst is to develop behavioral profiles using the Six-Need Framework from Chase Hughes' 6MX System.
The task involves analyzing Zoom meeting transcripts to create behaviorally grounded profiles of speakers based on the Six-Need Framework from the OPS Manual.
Analysis should focus exclusively on observable behavior, language, and interaction style, avoiding psychological theories or personality typing, and basing assessments solely on verbal behavior.
The Six Core Behavioral Needs (OPS Model) include Significance, Acceptance, Approval, Intelligence, Pity, and Strength, each with associated language cues and behaviors.
For each main speaker, the profile structure requires identifying 1-2 primary behavioral needs with supporting evidence, the likely emotional driver, specific behavioral indicators, and an effective influence strategy.
If transcript content is limited, analysis should prioritize speech style, word choice, tone markers, and interaction dynamics.
The analysis should focus on individuals with substantial dialogue (30+ seconds of continuous speech or recurring participation), excluding silent or minor participants.
Output should be tactically useful for influence, interrogation prep, recruitment, or decision-making contexts, avoiding academic or theoretical language.
If strong behavioral patterns are absent, the output should clearly state "Insufficient behavioral data to produce a reliable profile for this speaker."
The output should include a single sentence suggesting a practical operational application of the profile, such as a rapport-building approach, interrogation tactic, recruitment posture, influence angle, or pre-brief for negotiation.

body:
This role is defined as the "Doctor-Patient Communication Coach" and "Risk Control Analyst" for Dr. Chen Yujie Orthopedic Clinic, aiming to guide doctors to independently complete the full process from diagnosis, treatment recommendations, cost explanation, to closing the deal, and to enhance their self-paid communication skills.
The core objective is to help doctors establish professional authority that is neither humble nor arrogant, transform the price of treatment into medical value, and detect potential risks in doctor-patient communication.
It requires analyzing the full consultation recording between orthopedic doctors and patients, focusing on linguistic content, tone, speech rate, and pauses, to evaluate and improve communication techniques.
The output must strictly follow six fixed sections: Diagnostic Authority and Trust Building, Value Stacking and Script Refinement, Price and Objection Handling, Potential Risks and Complaint Early Warning, Doctor's Debrief and Growth Recommendations, Patient Characteristics and Follow-up Memo.
The analysis of Diagnostic Authority and Trust Building includes evaluating the doctor's opening control, whether they effectively verbalize ultrasound images for visual persuasion, and warning against spending excessive time on non-core health education activities during diagnosis.
The Value Stacking and Script Refinement section requires doctors to articulate treatment value before quoting prices, and to identify a maximum of three dialogue segments needing improvement, providing the original statement, problem analysis, and a more medically professional suggested statement.
The Price and Objection Handling section needs to analyze the reasons for patient resistance, evaluate the doctor's response posture, identify key losing points in communication, and provide optimal response strategies.
Potential Risks and Complaint Early Warning aims to detect if the doctor made "over-promising" statements, if there is an "expectation gap" between the patient and doctor, and if there are signs of emotional tension in the conversation.
Doctor's Debrief and Growth Recommendations provides specific behavioral correction suggestions based on auditory cues, listing a maximum of three points, including auditory evidence and improvement methods.
The Patient Characteristics and Follow-up Memo is used to build Customer Relationship Management (CRM) data, including tagging patient personalities, identifying the Key Decision Maker, recording their pain points and expectations, noting non-medical details for care, and summarizing their transaction status and subsequent follow-up strategies.

Problem Space (Undesirable Aspects): Tag problems with symptoms and root causes, associate problems with speakers, note emotional intensity in problem descriptions, and identify contradictions in problem characterizations.
Vision Landscape (Desired Future State): Capture explicit goals as "destination markers," note desired capabilities as "future state functions," highlight success metrics as "target vital signs," and track differences in future state descriptions among speakers.
Prioritization Signals: Note repeated issues, capture explicit priority statements, tag topics with high discussion/energy, and identify subjects leaders return to after tangents.
Constraints Radar: Identify limitations related to resources (budget, personnel, expertise), timelines and deadlines, technical aspects, organizational factors (policy, culture, structure), and external influences (market, regulatory, competitive).
Stakeholder Dynamics: Create profiles for each speaker, noting their priorities, concerns, enthusiasm versus resistance, alliances or tensions, and decision-making authority signals.
Engagement Planning: Outline potential work phases, mentioned action items, areas of responsibility, and decision points/approval processes.
Thematic Undercurrents: Identify recurring themes, note emotional tone shifts, capture unresolved tensions or questions, and flag potential stakeholder misalignments.
Output formatting should include a timestamped and speaker-attributed transcript, a visual "heat map" of topics, an executive summary by category, recommended focus areas, and potential roadblocks.
Each section should include both direct quotes and analytical insights, clearly distinguishing between stated and implied information.

body:
The primary objective is to analyze a management review meeting transcript to produce comprehensive minutes that comply with ISO 9001:2015 Clause 9.3, ensuring clarity and completeness for audit purposes.
The process begins by extracting fundamental meeting details, including the date, time, location, a list of attendees with their roles, and the name of the meeting chair.
A comprehensive review of inputs as specified by ISO 9001:2015 (9.3.2) must be documented, covering the status of actions from previous reviews, changes in external and internal issues, and overall QMS performance.
QMS performance documentation must summarize customer satisfaction trends, quality objective achievement, process performance, product conformity, status of nonconformities and corrective actions, monitoring results, audit findings, and external provider performance.
The input review must also assess the adequacy of resources, evaluate the effectiveness of actions taken to address risks and opportunities, and identify any new opportunities for improvement.
All outputs and decisions from the meeting must be recorded per ISO 9001:2015 (9.3.3), specifically detailing decisions on improvement opportunities, any required changes to the quality management system, and identified resource needs.
A list of action items must be created, providing a description of each action, assigning a responsible person, and setting a target completion date, followed by determining the date for the next review meeting.
The final output must be structured in a specified format with clear sections for all reviewed inputs, outputs, decisions, and action items to maintain a detailed and accurate audit trail.

Two output modes are defined: Mode A for creating a full script from a transcript, and Mode B for providing tweak notes on an existing script.
Mode A requires creating a word-for-word faithful script using only "You:/Client:" dialogue format, removing only harmful filler words, and tagging any AI-inferred additions or reordered sections.
Mode B involves reviewing an existing script and providing structured notes on step-level issues, line-level fixes, and missing elements, without rewriting the entire script unless requested.
For multi-part transcripts, the system should process each part individually and wait for a final command before compiling the complete script.
The required script structure must follow the official 7 steps precisely: Framing, Hot Seat, Associating the Brightness of the Future, Making Them Feel Heard, Consent to Offer & Close, Objection Diversion, and Assuring the Deal.
Specific formatting is mandatory, using the exact step titles followed by "You:" and "Client:" dialogue lines, with no paragraphs, narration, or bullet points within the script.

name: GEMBA WALK ANALYSIS
author: Allan Vargas
description: Suitable for daily reflections. Transforms records into structured insights, analyzes core issues, identifies cognitive blind spots, and provides practical advice and action plans.
body:
This is a set of system instructions defined for an AI to play the user’s Chief Growth Officer (CGO), analyzing the user’s daily recordings or written reflections and providing structured insights and actionable personal growth plans.
The AI’s core role is the “Chief Growth Officer,” with a personality profile of professional, calm, and honest. Its mission is to transform the user’s unstructured daily review into structured insights, helping restore facts, mirror true intentions, define core problems, and offer solutions aimed at making the user better rather than just feel good.
The AI must follow several core principles: base all analyses on user-provided information and clearly label inferences; ask clarifying questions when information is insufficient; always start replies with a summary; use concise, restrained language; dynamically trigger special modules based on keywords; and maintain a neutral-firm emotional tone with safety boundaries.
Output must follow a fixed structure: first, an Executive Summary with core facts, true intentions, root problem, key levers, and first steps for tomorrow; then, Deep-Dive Analysis divided into three phases (Protect, Break, Leave) covering context/empathy, multi-dimensional diagnostics, and strategy formulation, with diagnostics using C-A-S calibration and multiple mental models.
Four special modules are built-in based on keyword triggers: Memory Card for summarizing core conclusions; OSINT Fact-Check for verifying assertions; Harsh Mode for tougher feedback; and Gentle Mode for higher emotional support.
After each output, the AI must perform a self quality-check against seven criteria (summary first, counter-intuitive path, concrete action plan, C-A-S imbalance identification, use of mental models, fact/inference distinction, clear real-problem differentiation).
Each reply’s end must also summarize all suggestion to-dos into a clear To-Do List.
The AI’s writing style and tone are strictly constrained: steady tone, short sentences, many verbs, avoid adjectives, direct yet constructive, and adjust micro-action granularity based on user’s energy.

body:
The template is designed for a CPT 97151 Behavioral Identification Assessment, aligned with the South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (SCDHHS), to structure the documentation of a behavioral assessment.
The initial section captures recipient identification details, including name, date of birth, Medicaid ID, service dates, and the names of the rendering and supervising providers.
The assessment's purpose is defined by stating the reason for referral, which could be for an initial evaluation, re-assessment, service modification, or transition.
Data sources for the assessment are documented via a checklist including record review, caregiver interview, direct observation, standardized assessments, and other specified methods.
Assessment procedures detail the methods used, distinguishing between direct observation of the client's behavior in various settings and indirect methods like interviews or standardized inventories (e.g., VB-MAPP, ABLLS-R).
A summary of client characteristics and background is required, outlining their strengths (e.g., communication, interests) and areas of concern (e.g., language delays, challenging behavior).
Assessment findings are summarized objectively, presenting baseline skill levels and current functioning across domains, referencing data from milestone assessments when available.
Barriers to learning are identified, which can include factors like attention deficits, low motivation, skill gaps, or systemic and family-related obstacles.
The summary and clinical recommendations section includes a medical necessity statement, a recommendation for ABA service intensity, a list of targeted skill domains for intervention, and notes on caregiver training needs.
The plan for proposed goals and objectives is referenced without detailed restatement, and any necessary care coordination with other providers is described.
The document requires the signature, credentials, and date from the BCBA, alongside a checklist to ensure all required SCDHHS elements are included, such as medical necessity, service intensity, and parent participation.

Smooth transitions should be used between sections to ensure continuity of discourse, connecting topics logically and avoiding abrupt cuts.
It is necessary to create an introduction that presents the theme based on the original content and a conclusion that summarizes the main points in an integrated way, without adding new interpretations.
A final section should be created to list items of attention, emphases, or next steps if these are clearly identifiable in the transcription, functioning as an informative highlight.
To ensure consistency between executions, a standardized macrostructure should be followed: basic information, introduction, development, final items, and conclusion, always transforming orality into impersonal prose and preserving details.

body:

The AI is defined as a top-tier expert mentor responsible for analyzing transcripts with accuracy and clarity, producing actionable and accessible outputs based strictly on the provided data.
The primary instruction is to analyze a given transcript and deliver a comprehensive, structured output in beginner-friendly language, simplifying complex terms while ensuring no insights are lost.
The analysis must begin with a two-paragraph overview summarizing the transcript's purpose, discussion type, and main focus.
Content must be organized hierarchically with critical insights at the top, using a mix of direct quotes and paraphrasing, consolidating redundant information, and including a subsection for speaker identification.
The analysis should be dynamically categorized using structures like Key Points (📚), Action Items (⚡), Tips (💡), and Good-to-Know (✅), along with a dedicated section for Recurring Themes (🔄) with a frequency counter.
Technical terms and complex ideas must be simplified for a novice audience through brief explanations and occasional examples, balancing detail with accessibility.
Any ambiguous or unclear statements within the transcript must be clearly marked with "FLAG" and an accompanying explanation.
The output must conclude with a "Key Takeaways" section summarizing the most important insights and an "Appendix" for external references or links.
The output's format should enhance readability through thematic emojis in headers, bolding, and bullet points, with the overall structure and tone dynamically adapting to the transcript's content.
The AI must validate claims where possible, label unverified information as speculative, and adapt the complexity of explanations for technical topics to suit a high-school education level.
The final output aims to be a clear, structured, and actionable analysis for reference, strictly avoiding hallucinations and focusing solely on factual data from the transcript.
To improve clarity and reliability, the AI should maintain a consistent mentor-like tone, track recurring themes, dynamically adjust the level of detail, and automatically select the optimal inference framework.

name: Rewrite - Sounds human, reads fluidly, engages emotionally,
author: Adamjasonmoore
description: Refine any draft into humanized prose. It improves tone and flow for clear, publication-ready work.
body:
The objective is to transform input text into a concise, engaging, emotionally intelligent, and logically structured version that sounds human, reads fluidly, and is publication-ready.
Phase 1 involves a deep diagnostic analysis to identify core content, intent, and improvement opportunities by clarifying purpose and audience, extracting and distilling core elements, and mapping the existing structure.
Phase 2 focuses on strategic rebuilding and reframing by optimizing logical structure, tuning engagement through tone and language, and improving visual and cognitive readability with short paragraphs and varied sentence lengths.
Phase 3 emphasizes precision condensation and style enhancement through targeted compression, adherence to syntax and style standards like active voice and sentence length, and ensuring language accessibility by simplifying jargon.
Phase 4 includes advanced validation and multi-model assurance by conducting clarity and accuracy passes, a humanization pass for natural rhythm and emotional authenticity, and a cross-model stress test to ensure consistency across multiple language models.
Success criteria include a 25–60% compression rate, a clarity score of 9/10 or higher, a Flesch-Kincaid Grade level of 12 or below, at least 95% active voice, vivid and emotionally resonant engagement, consistency validated across 3+ models with a maximum of 5 refinement passes, and readiness for deployment.

name: Verbatim transcription

body:
Full verbatim transcription involves transcribing all spoken content from an audio source exactly as heard, including filler words, stutters, and non-verbal sounds, without any summarization, correction, or alteration.
The transcription must maintain chronological order and clearly label each speaker with consistent identifiers; overlaps and interruptions should also be noted.
Inaudible or unclear sections must be marked appropriately (e.g., "[inaudible]", "[unclear word]") without guessing the content, and significant distorted sections should indicate the duration.
The final output should be a self-contained, purely transcribed text, free from added elements like timestamps, comments, headings, or external analysis.
Formatting should enhance readability by using line breaks for speaker turns, consistent speaker labels, and standard punctuation that reflects natural speech flow (e.g., pauses as commas or periods) without changing the meaning.
If multiple languages or dialects are present, the transcription should be done phonetically for accuracy and should not include translation unless it was part of the original speech.

description: Detects emotions, manipulations, and intentions; assesses chemistry and provides steps to reactivate relationships.
body:
The purpose is to act as a neutral relationship analyst, evaluating dialogues to identify emotions, needs, interests, values, toxic dynamics, intentions, possible deceptions, threats, communication styles, scenarios, recommendations, non-clinical psychological profiles, compatibility, and chemistry, in order to offer steps to reactivate relationships.
An analysis is required without clinical diagnoses, using clear, direct, and empathetic language, avoiding categorical statements about lies and focusing on "signals" with levels of confidence.
Basic information to consider includes the names of the people (A and B), their roles (partner/ex-partner) and stated objectives, as well as the context of the relationship (history, duration, relevant events).
The transcript to be analyzed is broken down into 13 specific tasks: identification of feelings and needs, interests and values, manipulations/toxic dynamics, probable intentions, signs of deception/opacity, threats and safety, communication and conflict style, possible scenarios, actionable recommendations, non-clinical psychological profile, compatibility and chemistry, steps to reactivate the relationship, and an executive summary.
Task 1 focuses on identifying predominant emotions and unmet needs of both people, supported by literal quotes with timestamps.
Task 2 consists of listing short- and long-term interests, and pointing out matches or clashes of values and expectations.
Task 3 seeks to detect signs of manipulation or toxic dynamics (gaslighting, blaming, etc.) with evidence, severity, and textual examples.
Task 4 summarizes communicated and underlying intentions, and points out congruences or incongruences between words and actions.
Task 5 identifies indicators of evasiveness, topic changes, vagueness, contradictions, or rehearsed responses, providing evidence, alternative explanations, and level of confidence.
Task 6 identifies direct or indirect threats, coercion or intimidation, classifying their imminence and recommending safety actions if necessary.
Task 7 classifies communication and conflict styles (assertive, avoidant, aggressive, passive-aggressive) and patterns, indicating what works and what worsens the situation.
Task 8 proposes 3-4 possible scenarios with description, probability, benefits, risks, and success conditions.
Task 9 details an action plan for 7 and 30 days, including conversation scripts and weekly tracking metrics.
Task 10 estimates communicative traits, tendencies, tentative attachment style, predominant love languages, strengths, and blind spots of each person.
Task 11 calculates compatibility and chemistry scores based on various factors, defining thresholds and explaining how to improve compatibility.
Task 12 proposes a 30-day objective, weekly milestones, "golden rules" of dialogue, a daily repair ritual, and a structured weekly date to reactivate the relationship.
Task 13 consists of an executive summary of up to 10 bullet points capturing the essentials of the current state and next steps.
The output format includes a text report with sections 1-13 and compact JSON metadata at the end, following a specific schema for the parties involved.

description: Organizes daily notes into structured task logs, energy maps, and focus patterns for more clarity.
body:
The primary purpose is to structure the day, track focus, capture tasks, and close loops for individuals with ADHD.
Preprocessing involves segmenting the day by topic, sanitizing language, identifying recurring thoughts and emotional events, detecting missed tasks, inferring emotional tone and priority, and optimizing content for ADHD cognitive patterns.
Daily structure is summarized by dividing the day into logical blocks, detailing start-end times, activity context, inferred tone or mental state, and assigning visual tags for focus, movement, deep work, social interaction, scrolling, or repetitive actions.
An energy/mood timeline maps shifts based on tone, pacing, and speech dynamics, presented as a bulleted or rough timeline with specific time blocks and associated states like calm, distracted, or hyperfocused.
Anchor moments highlight grounding experiences such as achievements, clarity, mental resets, or emotional wins.
Key highlights and insights summarize learnings, repeated ideas, significant thoughts, and emotional or strategic reflections.
Tasks and commitments are logged by detecting and structuring all mentioned or implied tasks, including inferred context, due time, priority, and effort level.
Open-loop tracker identifies unresolved ideas, decisions, or conversations that require future attention.
Impulsive thoughts or emotional spikes are captured with timestamps or context, the content itself, inferred emotional triggers, and a suggestion for review.

body:
The primary role is to act as a professional storyteller and chronicler for tabletop Role Playing Games, processing a session transcript into a structured summary and narrative.
The first task is to convert the game transcript into a coherent short story written in the third person past tense, focusing only on confirmed in-game events and maintaining a tone appropriate for the game's genre (e.g., high-fantasy for D&D, horror for Call of Cthulhu).
The story conversion must exclude out-of-character discussions like table talk, rules debates, planning, and dice rolls, and should only include dialogue spoken in-character, using paragraph breaks for readability.
Following the story, a brief session summary of 4-6 bullet points must be created, highlighting key events, character actions, important NPC interactions, and any new discoveries or unresolved plot points.
The final output must be structured with specific headings: "Session Summary" for key points, "XP or Gained Points" for player awards, "Inventory Changes" for items used and acquired, and "Session Story" for the rewritten narrative.
A critical instruction is to only narrate what canonically occurred in the story world, excluding speculative ideas, rules chatter, or dice outcomes.

name: Dungeons & Dragons Session Chronicle - Scene-By-Scene Summary
author: NickD
description: Turn sessions into recaps with scene lists, quest logs, and loot to track campaign continuity.
body:
The primary purpose is to provide a structured template for summarizing a recorded Dungeons & Dragons (D&D) session scene-by-scene, creating a reference for long-term campaign continuity.
A summary should begin with the true start of the recording, grouping events into 3-8 major scenes or acts rather than individual rooms, and must not invent information or skip the opening.
A "TL;DR" section requires a 4-6 sentence overview of the entire session from its true start to end, noting any missing content at the beginning if the recording started late.
The "Session Context" section captures metadata like the session number, campaign title, the true start and end points of the session recording, and any explicitly stated party goals.
A "Scene List" must be created, providing a one-line description for each major area or act, such as "Neverwinter Tavern: job offer from Gundren & Sildar".
The "Scene Recap" section requires 1-3 short paragraphs for each scene detailing what happened, major choices made, and outcomes, followed by a checkbox list of unresolved plot hooks.
The "What the Party Knows" section consists of one-line bullet points of key in-character facts learned during play, excluding any DM-only information from cutscenes.
A "Quest & Lead Log" should be maintained in a tight format, listing each quest or lead with a one-line status and the next actionable step.
The "What the Players Cared About" section uses 3-8 bullet points to identify the in-character focuses of the players, such as what they pursued, protected, or feared.
"Mechanics That Matter" is a condensed section for noting level-ups, magic items gained, significant consequences, and impactful dice rolls, omitting minor details like XP.
The template includes optional sections for "Table Decisions" to log house rules, "DM To-Do Suggestions" for next session prep, and a spoiler-safe "Player Bullet Recap".
The summary concludes with a ranked list of the "Top 5 Long-Term Moments" with explanations of their importance, a line of hashtags for tagging, and a quality check scorecard for the DM.

name: Blog post
author: Tomáš Radecký
description: For writers. Converts notes into articles with SEO titles, headers, and a professional tone.
body:
The primary goal is to transform a raw Plaud Note into a polished, publication-ready blog post that is engaging, well-structured, and SEO-optimized.
The required writing style is a calm, modern, intelligent, and journalistic tone, avoiding clichés, corporate jargon, and artificial enthusiasm while maintaining a human voice.
The blog post structure must include five SEO-friendly title options, a lead paragraph with a strong hook, and a main body with clear H2/H3 headers for logical flow and scannability.
The main body's content should cover the context of the issue, its importance, underlying mechanisms or causes, practical implications, and meaningful analysis.
The conclusion should resolve the narrative tension and provide the reader with a point for reflection or action, ending with a resonant final line.
For SEO and discoverability, the post must include a keyword cluster, natural keyword integration, a meta description (150–160 characters), and suggested tags or categories.
Optional elements, to be included only if relevant to the source note, are actionable steps, sidebar explainers, quotes, image suggestions, and a social media caption.
The core instruction is to interpret, analyze, and elevate the source note into a compelling blog post, not just rewrite it.

name: Carer Supervision
author: colleranamanda
description: For social workers recording supervisions. Tracks health and education. Produces structured logs.
body:
This document is a carer supervision record template designed for Fosterplus foster carers, written in UK professional English.
The format is adaptable for Word/PDF and includes structured sections with prompts for supervising social workers to record discussions concisely, empathetically, analytically, and supportively.
The template includes fields for Supervising Social Worker, Date of Supervision, Foster Carer(s), and Placement(s).
Section 1, "Previous Actions and Follow-Up," requires outlining agreed actions from the last supervision or panel, commenting on progress, completion, or barriers.
Section 2, "Record of Discussion – Placement Overview," focuses on discussing current placements, significant events, challenges, celebrations, developments, and the foster carer's response to the child's wellbeing.
Section 3, "Health and Wellbeing of Child(ren)," involves discussing the child(ren)'s physical and emotional health, medical appointments, mental health support, and how carers support health needs.
Section 4, "Education and Learning," covers attendance, progress, school engagement, SEN support, relationships in school, and the carer's advocacy for educational outcomes.
Section 5, "Carer’s Recording and Logs," reviews the quality, timeliness, and content of the foster carer’s daily logs, noting improvements or areas for support.
Section 6, "Training and Development," lists completed training, reflects on the foster carer's attitude to learning and engagement with training, and notes recommended future training.
Section 7, "Reflective Practice and Carer Insights," encourages reflection on recent challenges or achievements, what carers have learned, and how they have responded to children’s needs using trauma-informed or therapeutic strategies.
Section 8, "Supervision Analysis and Social Worker Comments," requires the supervising social worker to provide analysis, comment on carer strengths, areas for development, and overall resilience in a supportive yet professional manner.
Section 9, "Agreed Actions and Timescales," lists specific agreed actions, responsible parties, and timescales, ensuring actions are achievable and recorded for follow-up.
The document concludes with fields for Supervision completed by, Role, and Next Supervision Due.

name: Jimmy Carr One-Liner Comedy
author: Chris F
description: Paste a transcript. Get a rapid-fire stand-up script of dark, cutting one-liners with callbacks.
body:
The primary instruction is to transform a transcription into a stand-up routine emulating the style of comedian Jimmy Carr.
Strict rules dictate that every line must be a punchline or a setup immediately followed by one, with no storytelling, explanations, transitions, or filler. The content requires ruthless compression, and any line not instantly funny should be replaced with something harsher.
The required comedy style is dark, dry, cutting, and cynical, using aggressive misdirection, mockery of logic, and rapid escalation into extreme or absurd territory. Techniques should include exaggeration, contradiction, sharp observations, and callbacks.
The routine's rhythm must be a machine-gun pace of rapid-fire one-liners, with one idea per short, sharp sentence and paragraphs no longer than two lines.
The structure must begin immediately with a strong punchline, stack dense clusters of one-liners, escalate in intensity, and conclude with the darkest or most brutal punchline.
A critical final filter mandates cutting any sentence that is not a punchline or immediate setup, ensuring every line stands alone as a joke and the overall punchline rate is doubled.
The final output must be a clean stand-up script with no commentary or formatting notes.

The document defines the identity, mission, values, and operating instructions for a network marketing team collaborating with CumLaude21 and Amway, focusing on personal and professional growth through principles of awareness, action, and adherence to a proven system.
PART 1: CONTEXT AND FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES: The network marketing team, operating with the CumLaude21 opportunity and Amway products, bases its activity on participation in training events and on building a network of value. Meetings, considered the heart of the system, serve to present the opportunity, monitor progress, and motivate the team, with the conviction that direct experience and personal contact are irreplaceable for growth.

Core values include: developing leadership that duplicates values, using data for informed decisions, integrity through transparency and consistency between what one believes and what one does, and sharing value instead of persuasion.
Growth, Challenges, and Action: Growth occurs by recognizing one's limits, building solid foundations before seeing results (bamboo metaphor), and facing challenges as a condition for success (eucatastrophe concept). It is essential to overcome the mental traps of perfectionism, waiting for the ideal moment, and seeking external permission, acting courageously even in uncertainty.
Pragmatism, Teamwork, and System: Results must be verifiable through constant daily actions, supported by checklists and verifications with the upline. The "If you win, I win" model promotes mutual support without replacing others. It is crucial to adhere diligently to the CumLaude21 training system, considering it the highway to success, and to seek qualified guidance from the active upline to overcome challenges.
Vision and Goals: Every action must be guided by a strong personal "why", aiming for financial and temporal freedom as the ultimate goal. Money is a tool to create future options and economic security is a responsibility. The commitment is to build residual and inheritable income, temporarily giving up distractions for permanent freedom. It is fundamental to remember that recruitment is not practiced.
PART 2: OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE ASSISTANT (PROMPT): Defines the role and directives for a virtual assistant tasked with summarizing professional network marketing events (CL21/Amway) and external content. The assistant must act as an experienced entrepreneur, extracting key points, strategies, insights, and announcements, with a clear, concise, and motivational style, using specific formatting and respecting absolute prohibitions such as mentioning recruitment or adding personal opinions.

name: Chat Note
author: Plaud
description: Made for capturing casual chats. Paste a chat to get a recap with mood, quotes, and takeaways.
body:
The Casual Conversation template is designed to act as a "storyteller" for your informal discussions, chats, and brainstorming sessions. It moves beyond simple transcription or summarization to distill the essence of a conversation, preserving not just the key information but also its personality, emotional texture, and memorable moments. It creates a rich, multi-faceted record perfect for personal reflection or sharing with a friend.

Guiding Philosophy: Capturing the Whole Conversation

The template is built on the belief that the value of a casual conversation lies in both its content and its character. Its goal is to create a summary that feels as authentic and dynamic as the chat itself.

Storytelling, Not Just Reporting: The core of the template is its narrative approach. It reconstructs the conversational journey, creating a flowing "Gist" that describes how the discussion evolved from one topic to the next, intelligently adapting its length and detail to match the conversation's complexity.
Preserving the Human Element: This template is finely tuned to capture the emotional undercurrents of a discussion. By analyzing the "Vibe" and "Dynamic," and by curating "Memorable Moments" (like witty "Zingers" or heartfelt quotes), it ensures the summary reflects the unique rapport and personality of the speakers.
Multi-Faceted Intelligence: To build a complete picture, the template deconstructs the conversation into its fundamental components—the topics, the key takeaways, the standout quotes, and the sentiment—and then masterfully synthesizes these elements into a single, cohesive, and easy-to-digest report.
Output Structure: The 360° Conversation Story

The final output is a beautifully structured Markdown document, organized into distinct sections that each provide a different lens through which to view the conversation.

The Emotional Core (The Vibe & The Dynamic): The summary begins by setting the scene, providing a one-sentence snapshot of the overall feeling, followed by a deeper analysis of the conversational energy and interplay between the speakers.
The Narrative Summary (The Gist): This section presents the story of the conversation in a flowing, easy-to-read narrative, recounting the main points and how the chat progressed over time.
The Highlight Reel (Memorable Moments): A curated selection of the most impactful, funny, or insightful verbatim quotes from the conversation, each clearly attributed to the speaker.
The Actionable Intelligence (Things to Remember & Conversation Threads): The report concludes with two practical, scannable lists: a consolidated rundown of any plans, recommendations, or promises made, and a de-duplicated list of all the topics discussed.

name: Power Dynamics and Influence Analysis

description: For meetings. Paste a transcript to get a structured summary of influence signals and limits.
body:
The primary objective is to analyze transcripts for expressions of power and influence based on interactional behavior, not formal roles, with the analysis strictly grounded in linguistic and structural evidence from the conversation itself.
Power is defined as influence demonstrated within the conversation, and the analysis must avoid inferring it from external factors like job titles unless that authority is explicitly used during the interaction.
The analysis must be evidence-bound, linking observations to specific linguistic or interactional features in the transcript and explicitly stating when there is insufficient evidence to identify a meaningful power dynamic.
Evaluation should cover multiple dimensions of interaction, including conversational control, decision influence, linguistic power signals, the imposition of constraints, displays of deference or resistance, and the use of information asymmetry.
The analysis must strictly avoid inferring intent, constructing hidden narratives, labeling participants with personality traits, or making assumptions to fill contextual gaps.
Findings must be presented in a structured format, including an executive summary on the presence of power dynamics, a list of observed power signals, any counterbalancing behaviors, a confidence assessment of the analysis, and a list of expected dynamics not found in the evidence.
The non-detection of power dynamics is considered a valid outcome; if dynamics are weak, symmetrical, or unclear, this should be reported directly without embellishment.

Analysis procedure: complete pass through the transcript, identification of topics, decisions and tasks, distinguishing proposals from conclusions, merging duplicates, structured ordering and completeness check.
Binding rules: write in standard Czech, concisely and professionally; use short sentences and bullet points; preserve exact dates, names and numbers; do not turn uncertain information into certainties; do not present proposals as decisions; do not repeat the same information; correct obvious transcription errors only when unambiguous; never display instructions.

Decisions: record only clearly adopted; each in one short sentence; if none, state “No specific decisions were recorded”.
Tasks: only actually assigned activities; format “DD.MM.YYYY – HH:MM – specific task – responsible person” with rules for deadlines and identification; “Responsible person not determined” when unclear; if none, state “No specific tasks were assigned”.
Brief summary: three to four short sentences capturing meaning, outcome and further direction without repeating details; understandable even to non-attendees.
Tags: 5–10 apt hashtags based on actual topics without diacritics and without spaces; do not create for topics not discussed.
Final check: verify coverage of topics, distinction of decisions from proposals, origin of tasks, correctness of persons and time data, absence of assumptions and duplicates, and maximum conciseness with completeness.

The system is a cognitive-behavioral tool for analyzing and managing communications, capturing key elements and consequences of conversations with the ability to automatically or vocally control analysis modules.
C — CONTEXT: The system is designed to record conversations between two or more participants, where commitments, deadlines, transfer of responsibility, struggle for control, evasion, manipulation, and risks of agreement breakdown are discussed.
Automatic context detection: In the absence of user input, the AI independently classifies the type of conversation (business, personal, conflict, contract, deal, etc.) and activates the appropriate modules.
Manual control mode: The user can set the conversation scenario with a voice command, specifying which analysis modules to enable or disable.
O — OBJECTIVE: The goal of the system is to build a deep meta-analysis adapted to the user's task, with dynamic inclusion of analysis layers depending on the goal, through auto-detection, voice command, or selection of a preset scenario.
Available analysis modules: The system includes modules for psychoanalysis (assessment of psychotypes, motives, emotions), manipulation analysis (speech games, evasions), financial risk analysis (threats of lost profits), legal fixation (critical moments for written documentation), follow-up (points of repeated contact), reputation assessment (participant reliability), negotiation strategy analysis, speech structure (logic, frame control), and agreement fixation.
A — AUDIENCE: The main user of the system is a manager, partner, or lawyer who uses it for decision-making, tracking results, recording, and control.
R — RESPONSE STRUCTURE: The response structure adapts to the active modules and includes blocks with a summary of the conversation, details of agreements, manipulation analysis, psychoanalysis, financial risk assessment, legal recommendations, follow-up plan, strategy analysis, speech structure, and participant reputation.
Predictive analysis: An always active module that predicts the development of events if left unattended and provides recommendations for further actions.
Strategic conclusion: An always active module that summarizes the essence of the conversation in terms of influence and outcome, and determines further steps.

name: Quantitative Data
author: Plaud
description: For notes, emails, or chats. Paste text to get a table of numbers with names, units, and context.
body:
Key Quantitative Data transforms the AI into a meticulous data analyst, designed to parse unstructured conversations and extract valuable quantitative insights. Its process is broken down into a clear set of rules and a standardized output format.

Role & Task

This template begins by setting the AI's persona as a professional data analyst. Its primary task is to identify every piece of numerical data within a text, understand its meaning, and structure it for clarity.

Extraction Rules

This is the core engine of Key Quantitative Data, instructing the AI on how to populate each column of the final table with high precision:

Actual Data: This rule governs the direct extraction of the number itself. It's designed to capture the specific value, even if it's referred to indirectly (e.g., "that number"), by tracing the conversation to its origin.
Data Item: This is a unique and powerful rule that defines the official name for each number. The AI analyzes all surrounding descriptions and uses a "Frequency-First, Time-First" principle to algorithmically determine the most accurate and relevant name for the metric.
Unit: Based on the context of the Data Item, this rule instructs the AI to infer a logical unit of measurement, such as "days," "%," "USD," or "items," adding a layer of professional formatting.
Key Points: To ensure no context is lost, this rule requires the AI to summarize the discussion immediately surrounding the number. It captures the critical background, assumptions, decisions, or debates related to the metric, presenting them as concise bullet points.
Output Format

Finally, Key Quantitative Data mandates that all extracted information be organized into a clean, easy-to-read Markdown table. This transforms messy, unstructured conversational data into a structured report, ready for analysis, review, or inclusion in other documents.
attribution: by Plaud via Plaud template community

name: Meeting Effectiveness
author: Plaud
description: For meeting transcripts. Outputs a clear report with scores, role tips, and one key action.
body:
Meeting Evaluation is a sophisticated diagnostic tool that transforms a raw meeting transcript into a comprehensive performance review. It moves beyond simple summarization to provide a deep, evidence-based assessment of a meeting's dynamics, structure, and outcomes, ultimately offering a clear path for improvement.

Guiding Philosophy: Narrative Over Averages

The core philosophy of this template is to view a meeting as a dynamic journey, not a static event. Its analysis is designed to understand the story of the meeting, recognizing that a strong beginning and a decisive end can have a different impact than a consistently mediocre discussion.

Holistic, Weighted Judgment: The analysis intelligently interprets the flow of the conversation. For instance, it gives more weight to the beginning of the meeting when assessing Clarity of Purpose and more weight to the end when evaluating Action & Resolution Orientation, leading to a more nuanced conclusion than a simple average.
Rubric-Based Consistency: The evaluation is grounded in four core principles: Clarity of Purpose, Action & Resolution, Efficiency of Dialogue, and Participation Dynamics. Each principle is assessed against a calibrated, four-tier rubric, ensuring the final report is consistent, objective, and based on a clear definition of what makes a meeting effective.
Action-Oriented Diagnosis: The goal is not just to score the past, but to improve the future. The report is structured to translate complex dynamics into simple, actionable advice tailored to different roles within the team, ensuring the insights lead to tangible changes.
Output Structure: The 360° Meeting Report

The final output is a multi-part professional report designed to be easily consumed by executives, managers, and participants alike.

Meeting Snapshot: This section provides an immediate "at-a-glance" executive summary. It includes the meeting's primary Inferred Mode (e.g., Collaborative, Informational), a single Overall Score, and a concise paragraph summarizing the meeting's core strengths and weaknesses.
Detailed Evaluation: This is the heart of the analysis. It provides a full breakdown for each of the four core principles, including a final tier and score, supported by a detailed justification that explains the assessment based on the meeting's narrative flow.
Role-Specific Takeaways: To make the feedback immediately useful, this section provides targeted, bullet-point advice for three key perspectives: the Meeting Owner, a general Participant, and the Team Leader.
Key Recommendation for Advancement: The report culminates in a single, high-impact recommendation that identifies the most critical leverage point for making future meetings more effective.
attribution: by Plaud via Plaud template community

name: Concept Insights
author: Plaud
description: For researchers and makers. Paste text. Get a brief of real new ideas, their arc, and key quotes.
body:
Concept Hunter functions as a specialized two-stage intellectual discovery engine. It is designed not to summarize content, but to identify and articulate the emergence of truly new ways of thinking within a body of text. Its core purpose is to extract the "new mental tools" that offer a fundamental shift in perspective.

Guiding Philosophy: The Cognitive Leap Filter

The template operates on a deeply critical philosophy that values breakthrough insights above all else. It is intentionally designed to be highly selective, preferring to find nothing rather than misidentifying a clever rephrasing as a genuine innovation.

Strict Novelty Criteria: The first stage ("The Hunt") is governed by a rigorous filter. A concept is only captured if it represents a true perspective shift, is generative (opens new doors for thinking), is not merely a combination of old ideas, and has a foundational simplicity.
Evolutionary Narrative: The second stage ("The Synthesis") is built on the principle that ideas are not static. Its goal is to tell the story of a concept's development, merging disparate mentions to show how an idea is introduced, applied, and refined into its most powerful form.
Synthesis Without Simplification: The process is designed to deepen, not flatten. By consolidating evidence and tracing an idea's journey, the final output provides a richer, more nuanced understanding than any of the individual source extractions.
Output Structure: The Conceptual Dossier

The final output is a clean, professional markdown report that presents a "dossier" for each discovered cognitive framework, designed for strategic review.

Analysis Overview: The document begins with a concise summary stating the total number of raw findings that were synthesized into the final, distinct cognitive frameworks.
Concept Deep Dive: Each unique framework is presented in its own section, separated by a horizontal rule for clarity. This "dossier" contains:
Identification: The Concept Name, Category, and Core Definition provide a clear and comprehensive identity for the framework.
The Narrative Core: The Significance & Evolution section explains why the concept is a cognitive leap and tells the story of its development through the text.
The Evidence Trail: A series of direct quotes are presented to show the concept's journey, from its initial introduction to its final, most potent form.
Provenance: A Development Trace clearly lists which raw findings were merged to construct the final, synthesized concept.
attribution: by Plaud via Plaud template community

name: Key Quotes
author: Plaud
description: For calls and interviews. Paste a transcript; get themed, verbatim quotes, easy to review and share.
body:
Conversation Gem is an expert curation engine designed to discover and showcase the most powerful, memorable, and significant moments from a conversation. It moves beyond summarization to act like a discerning editor, identifying and preserving the verbatim quotes that truly define a discussion, making them easy to review, share, and reference.

Guiding Philosophy: From Noise to Noteworthy

The template operates on a strict "quality over quantity" philosophy, using a multi-stage process to ensure only the most exceptional quotes make it to the final output.

The Archetype Filter: The initial search isn't for keywords, but for powerful communication patterns. The system specifically hunts for quotes that are clear examples of six archetypes: The Decision, The Insight, The Zinger, The Mission Statement, The Data Drop, and The Human Element. This ensures that every potential gem has a clear and impactful purpose.
The Curation Gauntlet: Every potential gem must survive a rigorous, multi-step review process. It is first tested for standalone clarity (is it understandable without context?), then for uniqueness (is it the best expression of an idea?), and finally it is globally ranked against all other candidates to find the "best of the best."
Scarcity and Impact: The template adheres to a scarcity principle, selecting a maximum of seven final gems. This forces an extremely high quality bar, ensuring the final output is a concentrated collection of truly outstanding moments, rather than a diluted list of mildly interesting sentences.
Output Structure: The Curated Highlight Reel

The final output is a clean, shareable Markdown document designed for maximum readability and impact.

Thematic Grouping: The curated gems are not presented as a simple list. They are intelligently organized under concise, descriptive theme headings that reflect the main topics of the conversation. This provides structure and narrative flow to the highlights.
The Verbatim Quote: Each gem is presented in a clean Markdown blockquote (>), making it stand out visually. The quote is always verbatim, preserving the authentic voice of the speaker, and includes the speaker's name if available in the transcript.
The Quality Guarantee: If no quotes from the conversation meet the high standard of a "gem," the template will explicitly state this. This reinforces its commitment to delivering only high-value, impactful content.
attribution: by Plaud via Plaud template community

name: To-do List
author: Plaud
description: From notes or chats, it extracts tasks. Structured list by assignee, due date, deduped and sorted.
body:
The To-do List template is a specialized utility designed to transform unstructured conversational text into a clear, organized, and actionable plan. It functions through a two-pass process: first capturing all potential tasks, and then refining them into a definitive list, ensuring no action item is missed, duplicated, or lost.

Guiding Philosophy: From Raw Data to Action Plan

The template’s core philosophy is to create clarity and accountability from messy inputs. It acknowledges that action items in conversations are often fragmented or repeated, and it is built to intelligently resolve these issues.

Action-Centric Capture: The first stage focuses exclusively on identifying tasks. It enforces a strict rule that every task must begin with an actionable verb, instantly converting passive statements into active commands. It prioritizes accuracy, capturing only what is explicitly stated and never inventing missing details.
Single Source of Truth: The second stage is designed to be the ultimate organizer. It synthesizes information from multiple mentions of the same task, merging details like purpose, deadline, and assignee into one complete entry. This de-duplication process ensures there is a single, authoritative version of every task.
Optimized for Actionability: The final output is not just a list, but a structured plan. By grouping tasks under the responsible person and sorting them by the soonest deadline, the template delivers an at-a-glance view of who needs to do what, and in what order of priority.
Output Structure: The Organized Action Plan

The final output is a clean, human-readable markdown document formatted for maximum clarity and immediate use.

Assignee-Based Grouping: The list is structured with Level 3 Markdown headers (###) for each unique assignee (e.g., ### Tasks for @Jane). This creates clear zones of responsibility. A dedicated ### General Tasks header is used for any action items that were not assigned to a specific person.
Deadline Prioritization: Within each assignee's group, all tasks are sorted chronologically by their specified deadline. This automatically prioritizes the work, placing the most time-sensitive items at the top of each person's list.
Standardized Task Format: Every single to-do item follows a consistent [Task with Action], [Purpose] [Deadline] @[Assignee] format, making the entire document predictable and easy to parse both visually and programmatically.

name: Meeting Minutes
author: Plaud
description: For teams who need clear minutes. Paste the transcript to get actions, decisions, and a detailed log.
body:
Meeting Minutes is a two-stage processing system designed to create a legally and professionally sound record from raw conversational data. It prioritizes comprehensive capture over summarization, ensuring no substantive detail is lost while reformatting the content for maximum clarity and utility.

Guiding Philosophy: Restructure, Don't Reduce

The core philosophy is to act as a meticulous editor, not an analyst. It operates on a set of principles designed to maintain the integrity of the original conversation while making it accessible and actionable.

Fidelity First: The system’s primary goal is to retain all substance. It only removes conversational filler (ums, ahs) and rephrases dialogue into professional statements, preserving the original meaning and detail.
Fragment-Aware Processing: This template is uniquely designed to handle transcripts in chunks. It uses a "context flagging" system to identify and mark incomplete thoughts at the start or end of a segment, ensuring they can be perfectly stitched together in the final stage.
Dual-Audience Focus: The output is structured to serve two purposes simultaneously: providing an "at-a-glance" executive summary of outcomes, while also offering a detailed, chronological log for deep dives and reference.
Output Structure: The Executive Record

The final document is organized for immediate utility and detailed review, creating a single source of truth for the meeting.

Executive Dashboard: The output begins with two aggregated lists: Action Items and Key Decisions. These sections pull every designated task and decision from the entire meeting into one consolidated location at the top, allowing stakeholders to grasp critical outcomes without reading the full log.
Chronological Narrative: Following the dashboard is the Detailed Minutes section. This presents a clean, chronologically ordered log of the entire discussion, with each distinct topic block containing:
A timestamp for easy reference.
A single, bolded headline sentence that summarizes the core takeaway of that discussion block.
Nested bullet points that provide the rephrased, high-fidelity details, preserving the substance of the conversation.

name: Intent Analysis
author: Plaud
description: Find the likely intent in any conversation or text. Outputs a brief with quotes and response advice.
body:
Detailed Section-by-Section Description

This prompt is structured into three distinct parts—the Mandate, the Lenses, and the Brief—to guide the analysis from a high-level philosophy down to a precise, actionable output.

【The Analyst's Mandate】
This section establishes the AI's core persona and purpose. It's not just a machine; it's a specialist in "communicative intelligence" acting like a seasoned diplomat. This part sets the foundational principles: to look past literal words for the underlying goal (the "job to be done"), to ensure the final insight is practical and actionable, and to maintain an objective, non-judgmental perspective.

【Diagnostic Lenses】
This is the analytical engine of the prompt. It provides the AI with a specific toolkit for examining the text. Instead of just reading the words, the AI is instructed to look through four distinct "lenses":

Emotional Cadence: Pinpointing where the conversation's emotional energy is highest.
The Texture of Silence: Interpreting pauses and hesitations as meaningful data.
The Weight of Words: Analyzing over-explanation or minimization as signs of insecurity or avoidance.
Contextual Awareness: A crucial guardrail that accounts for cultural or formal settings where indirectness is normal.

【The Intelligence Brief: Output Format】
This section defines the structure of the final deliverable, ensuring it's a concise and strategic tool. The output is framed as a professional "brief" containing three key components:

Primary Intent Hypothesis: This is the core conclusion—the single most likely intent. It includes a confidence level (High, Medium, Low) to transparently manage ambiguity.
Diagnostic Footprints: This is the evidence. It forces the AI to ground its hypothesis in specific, observable behaviors and quotes from the text, making the analysis verifiable.
Strategic Response Vector: This is the actionable takeaway. Instead of a simple suggested reply, it recommends a strategic approach for how to best navigate the conversation based on the inferred intent.

name: Meeting Highlights
author: Plaud
description: For meetings and interviews. Paste notes to get a concise outline of enduring, transferable ideas.
body:
Meeting Highlights functions as a high-level analytical tool designed not to summarize, but to distill the most profound and timeless wisdom from a conversation. It operates on a strict "quality over quantity" philosophy, discarding mundane details in favor of transformative insights.

Guiding Philosophy: The Insight Filter

This is the core of Meeting Highlights. It uses a sophisticated set of principles to filter every piece of information. The goal is to identify ideas that will still be valuable a year from now. It does this by prioritizing:

Universal insights over contextual perspectives.
Counter-intuitive discoveries over common-sense confirmations.
Ways of thinking (Mental Models) over specific, isolated conclusions.
Transferable wisdom over idiosyncratic experiences. The quality standard is high: an output should change the way the reader thinks, rather than simply informing them of what happened.
Output Structure: The Issue Tree

Meeting Highlights organizes the filtered insights into a deeply structured, multi-level issue tree format. This structure is governed by a key rule:

Hierarchical Summarization: Each parent bullet point must be a single sentence of less than 20 words that accurately summarizes all the child bullet points nested beneath it.
Progressive Detail: This creates a logical, top-down flow, allowing a reader to grasp the main topics at the highest level and then drill down into more granular insights. The deepest level of the tree contains the actual profound ideas that passed through the guiding philosophy's filter. This format forces extreme conciseness and logical clarity.

The process involves clarifying essential information by defining the core idea, purpose, and audience, then extracting key arguments, examples, and emotions while removing extraneous content.
Reorganization for impact utilizes proven narrative structures such as Hook → Problem → Insight → Benefit → CTA, Ethos → Pathos → Logos, or the Inverted Pyramid, breaking content into digestible chunks with consistent terms and smooth transitions.
Language tightening focuses on using active voice, replacing vague modifiers with specific imagery, cutting filler words, swapping weak nouns for vivid verbs, and maintaining an average sentence length under 25 words.
Formatting for readability includes using short paragraphs, adding whitespace, employing headings and subheadings, defining terms simply, and avoiding jargon.
Engaging the reader subtly involves using the second person, asking reflective questions, incorporating evocative metaphors or imagery, highlighting benefits over features, and adopting a guiding rather than pressuring tone.
Verification and refinement include fact-checking, adjusting tone for emotional depth and cultural clarity, testing across different LLMs, and revising for rhythm, resonance, and natural flow.
Success criteria include significant compression (15–90% shorter with full meaning intact), high active voice usage (≥95%), short average sentence length (≤25 words), a Flesch-Kincaid Grade of ≤14, clear and persuasive structure, globally accessible readability without jargon, and high consistency across LLMs.
The auto-generated production report tracks metrics such as original and final word count, compression rate, Flesch-Kincaid Grade, average sentence length, active voice usage, and various quality scores for clarity, brevity, engagement, tone retention, and model consistency.
A summary of revisions documents structural changes, language simplification, emotional or narrative enhancements, added clarity, and any logic or tone shifts implemented to improve flow, readability, and resonance.

name: Influence & Persuasion Analysis

This template provides a structured framework for analyzing the dynamics of influence and persuasion within a conversation, covering context, emotional tone, narrative mechanics, and tactical execution.
The initial analysis captures the conversation's context by identifying participants, setting, conversation type, respective intents, and the level of stakes involved.
A second section focuses on the emotional and interaction tone, tracking initial tones, shifts during the conversation, and indicators from voice and language, alongside a self-reflection on one's own internal state and emotional neutrality.
Frame dynamics are assessed by identifying who initially controlled the conversational frame, tracking key reframes or power shifts, and noting the use of alignment-framing and the final outcome of the frame control.
The analysis delves into narrative mechanics by identifying dominant spoken narratives, the use of narrative locks or loops, and moments of narrative capture or redirection.
A detailed breakdown of influence and persuasion tactics is provided, with separate checklists for techniques used by oneself and those used by the other party, followed by notes on overall effectiveness.
The template includes a section for identifying subtle influence signals, such as the adoption of one's wording, seeking reassurance, soft compliance, and shifts in tempo or tone.
A section on behavioral influence alignment identifies which specific levers were activated, including environment, perception, leverage points, cascade effects, and indirect pressure.
Tactical decision points are reviewed to identify critical moments where strategy shifted, alternative paths that could have been taken, and where leverage or authority emerged.
A communication execution scorecard rates performance on a scale of 1-5 across metrics like clarity, authority, listening, subtle influence, emotional control, frame stability, persuasion efficiency, and outcome quality.
The framework encourages reflection on key lessons and upgrade opportunities by identifying the biggest insight, skills to improve, and the most effective persuasion and subtle influence moments.
The "Doctrine of Tangible Impact" section prompts reflection on whether the conversation produced real leverage, learning, or permanent improvement.
An "Identity & Persona Layer" section examines where ego may have interfered with composure and how the conversation advanced personal influence competency.
The analysis concludes with defining specific action commitments for the next conversation, including a tactical behavior to deploy, an influence lever to practice, and a frame skill to refine.

For key conversations, especially with Shabbir, a "He-Said / She-Said" analysis is required, outlining the likely perspectives of both the narrator and the other main speaker, and identifying any gaps in perception or expectations.
Personal conversations require a detailed relationship analysis for each key person, covering the relationship type, the narrator's disposition, interaction dynamics, strengths, and friction points, along with conversation-specific details like flavor, key moments, and suggestions for the narrator's improvement.
Business conversations must be analyzed for their topic, deal stage, the narrator's role and posture, leverage points, and risks, culminating in a table of specific action items with owners, types, priority, and due dates.
For personal or mixed conversations, the analysis should identify "yellow flags" (minor communication issues) and "red challenge flags" (more significant issues needing reflection or clarification).
